noun: intention

Front:
глагол: желать
сущ.: желание
прил.: желанный
Back:
verb: desire / want
noun: desire
adj: desirable
→ I want to specialize in artificial intelligence.
→ This is a desirable skill for the program.

verb: attempt / try
noun: attempt
→ He attempted to fix the bug before deployment.
→ It was a serious attempt to improve latency.

Front:
сущ.: обязанность
прил.: обязанный
глагол: обязывать
Back:
noun: obligation
adj: obliged / obligated
verb: oblige
→ The rules create an obligation to submit all documents.
→ Applicants are required to meet the deadline.

verb: perform
noun: performance
→ Pattern B shows who performs the action.
→ The team delivered a strong performance under pressure.

verb: expect
noun: expectation
→ I expect to finish the module by Friday.
→ The result exceeded my expectations.

verb: agree
noun: agreement
→ They agreed to collaborate on the robotics project.
→ We reached an agreement on the project scope.

verb: refuse
noun: refusal
→ She refused to sign the contract without revisions.
→ His refusal slowed the whole process.

verb: promise
noun: promise
→ They promised to help with the integration.
→ He made a promise to deliver by Friday.

verb: afford
adj: affordable
→ I can't afford to wait another semester.
→ This option is more affordable for students.

verb: pretend
→ He pretended to understand the proof.
→ Don't pretend to know what you haven't tested.

verb: seem
→ We seem to have underestimated the effort.
→ The fix seems to have worked.

verb: appear
noun: appearance
→ The system appears to have recovered after the restart.
→ His calm appearance helped in the interview.

verb: encourage
noun: encouragement
→ She encouraged us to participate in the hackathon.
→ Your encouragement helped me keep going.

verb: allow
noun: allowance / permission
→ The program allows students to use the research lab.
→ They were given permission to access the server room.

verb: persuade
noun: persuasion
→ He persuaded me to join the motorsport team.
→ It took some persuasion to change my mind.

verb: require
noun: requirement
→ The university requires applicants to submit a motivation letter.
→ This course has strict entry requirements.

verb: avoid
→ He avoided mentioning his previous employer.
→ Avoid deploying on Friday without full testing.

Front:
глагол: возражать; не возражать
сущ.: возражение
Back:
verb: mind
noun: objection
→ Would you mind waiting outside for a moment?
→ I don't mind helping with the review.

verb: suggest
noun: suggestion
→ She suggested applying for a research internship.
→ That was a useful suggestion.

verb: consider
noun: consideration
→ He considered transferring to a research-focused track.
→ Cost is an important consideration.

verb: practice
noun: practice
→ I practice speaking English every morning.
→ Daily practice builds confidence.

verb: deny
noun: denial
→ She denied deleting the production database.
→ He was in denial about the bug.

verb: admit
noun: admission
→ He admitted making a mistake in the deployment.
→ His admission saved the team a lot of time.

phrase: get used to + -ing
→ She is getting used to working under tight deadlines.
→ You'll get used to reading academic papers in English.

phrase: look forward to + -ing
→ I look forward to starting my CS program at ZJU.
→ We look forward to hearing from the admissions office.

phrase: object to + -ing
→ He objected to being reassigned without notice.
→ Many students objected to changing the exam format.

phrase: admit to + -ing
→ I admit to underestimating the complexity of the project.
→ She admitted to ignoring the security warning.

phrase: devote ... to + -ing / noun
→ We are devoted to building reliable systems.
→ He devotes most of his time to research.

phrase: prefer ... to ...
→ I prefer working in small teams to working in huge corporations.
→ She prefers Python to Java for prototyping.

phrase: in addition to + noun / -ing
→ In addition to algorithms, the program covers systems design.
→ In addition to studying, he works on open-source projects.
